vo.en: Stop touching things in the store.

visual.description: A close-up of a man's hand reaching out and grasping a luxury item on a high-end store shelf.

vo.en: Retailers know that holding an item for thirty seconds flips a psychological switch in your head.

visual.description: A man standing in an aisle, holding a sleek box and examining it closely with focused eyes.

vo.en: Suddenly, you don't just want it. You feel like you already own it. This is the Endowment Effect.

visual.description: A man looking at a new gadget in his hands with a very proud and satisfied expression.

vo.en: But here is the creepy part: putting it back actually triggers physical pain in your brain.

visual.description: Close-up of a hand slowly and reluctantly letting go of a product and pulling away from a shelf.

vo.en: Your subconscious treats the object like your own property. Leaving without it feels like a personal loss.

visual.description: An abstract 3D animation of neural pathways lighting up or a brain scan glowing with blue light.

vo.en: Test it right now. Pick up any object nearby. Hold it. That ownership shift is the trap.

visual.description: A first-person perspective of a hand lifting a smartphone or a ceramic mug from a desk.

vo.en: Subscribe for tomorrow's brain test and comment GOT ME if you felt it, which is exactly why

visual.description: A close-up of a mouse cursor clicking a red subscribe button on a screen followed by a man nodding.
